title: Event delegation for dynamic lists
when: A list, table or grid gets items added and removed at runtime and every item needs clicks, edits or keys handled.
prompt:
Goal: One listener on a stable container handles current and future items, routed by data attributes, with no leaks.
Steps:
1. Attach one click listener (and change or input when items have fields) to a container that is never replaced, such as ul#items or tbody.
2. Resolve the target with event.target.closest("[data-action]"); return early when null.
3. Read btn.dataset.action and the item id from btn.closest("[data-id]").dataset.id.
4. Dispatch through a map: const actions = { delete: removeItem, toggle: toggleItem }; actions[action]?.(id).
5. Use <button type="button"> so Enter and Space work; handle Escape or arrows with one delegated keydown; delegate focus with focusin and focusout, which bubble.
Quality bar:
- Adding 1000 items adds zero listeners.
- Every action works from the keyboard.
- Button names include the item (Delete Milk).
Pitfalls:
- Comparing event.target directly, which fails when the click lands on an icon inside the button.
- Adding listeners inside the render loop, which stacks duplicates.
- Replacing the container on re-render and losing the listener.
Verify:
- [ ] Exactly one click listener for the list.
- [ ] closest() resolves targets.
- [ ] No inline onclick attributes.
- [ ] Buttons declare type="button".
Output: The list module (or app.js) with the delegated handler and action map; markup with data-id and data-action.

examples.input: delete buttons stop working on new todo items
examples.output: one click listener on ul#todos using closest("[data-action]") and an actions map
